title: 2025-09-30-geo-boundary-processing-and-kms-escrow-stratton-edutech
summary: Customer asked detailed questions about strict EU processing for student PII, whether Redwood can bind processing to EU-only nodes, KMS key ownership and escrow options, and a list of subprocessors. Redwood AE/SE walked through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SCCs, routing policies, and audit log retention. Agreed next steps: send up-to-date subprocessor inventory, SOC 2 + ISO artifacts, and a pilot config for EU region pinning with customer-managed keys.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood), Rachel Kim (Stratton CISO), Tom Ellis (Stratton Head of Platform), Priya Rao (Stratton Legal)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Rachel: Rachel Kim here, CISO at Stratton.
[00:11] Tom: Tom Ellis, Platform.
[00:13] Priya: Priya Rao, legal.
[00:15] Ava: Great, and from Redwood we have Samir and Lina as well. We're here to run through data residency, region pinning and some KMS questions you sent over. Roughly 45-60 minutes. Does that work?
[00:30] Rachel: Yep, our main ask is we need EU-only processing for student PII, and we need cryptographic controls so keys never leave EU for those objects. Also want subprocessor transparency.
[00:45] Samir: Understood. We'll cover host/dedicated/private trade-offs and what region pinning looks like operationally. Quick note: some transcriptions in my notes call Redwood Private "Redwood Privatee" — ignore that.
[01:10] Tom: We also must avoid cross-border backup snapshots going to US for that subset of data.
[01:25] Lina: Got it. I'll walk through how our routing and storage layers map to geography.

-- Topics: Region affinity, KMS key ownership, key escrow/escrow-like requests, subprocessors & SCCs, audit logs retention --

[02:00] Samir: On the hosted API, we have multi-region endpoints. By default traffic routes to nearest available region, but for customers with EU-only requirements we support region pinning which pins inference and storage to EU-exclusive clusters.
[02:20] Rachel: When you say "pins", does that cover logs, cached KV, model artifacts and backups? We need an assurance that none of those go to US subprocessors.
[02:35] Samir: For pinned projects we configure data plane components (inference nodes, KV cache, and object storage) in the specified region. Backups — we can configure retention and region for snapshots; for EU-only workload we can keep snapshots in EU buckets only.
[02:50] Tom: Is that automated or a manual config per project? We want it codified as infra-as-code so we can audit it.
[03:05] Ava: We provide a config spec that your infra team can pin in the console or via the infra API; it's stored in the control plane as a TenantConfig. If you prefer, for Dedicated/Private we can put that in your terraform modules.
[03:25] Priya: You mentioned "control plane" — does any part of the control plane carry PII? We require control plane metadata to be minimal and not include student IDs.
[03:40] Lina: The default hosted control plane catalogues config and metrics; we can set the control plane to store only hashed or tokenized identifiers. For the strictest case we recommend Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and never leaves your VPC.

[04:10] Rachel: Okay. Next KMS specifics: we need to ensure keys for EU-P1 data are customer-managed, and never exported to Redwood or to a US KMS. Do you have EU region KMS integrations? KMS + HSM?
[04:28] Samir: Yes: we integrate with cloud KMS providers in-region (e.g., AWS KMS eu-west-1, GCP KMS europe-west). For Private deployments we support BYOK with HSM-backed keys and can integrate with your key manager via standard APIs.
[04:45] Tom: What about key escrow? Our legal wants an escrow for disaster recovery but wants escrow to stay in EU. Can Redwood be the escrow holder?
[05:00] Ava: We can discuss a KMS escrow arrangement. Typically customers want either (a) customer-only keys, no escrow, (b) customer keys with an escrow held by a third party (law firm or custodian) or (c) a split-key approach. Redwood's standard hosted offering doesn't hold your customer keys by default — we can offer a contract addendum where Redwood holds sealed escrow copies in an EU HSM under strict access controls, but that likely sits under an enterprise agreement and additional fees.
[05:30] Priya: If Redwood holds escrow copies, what are the access conditions/audit controls? We need notarized access policies and attestation to the EU residency of the escrow.
[05:40] Lina: The escrow process we described would be documented in the KMS addendum. Access would require dual authorization, and all access events are logged to immutable audit logs with retention set per the contract. We can provide SOC 2 audit evidence for those controls.

[06:10] Rachel: About subprocessors — we received an older subprocessor list that showed some US infra providers for logging and monitoring. For EU-only projects we need either EU-based subprocessors or assurances they're not processing PII.
[06:28] Samir: We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor inventory. For EU region-pinned tenants we avoid US-based backup partners for pinned data; monitoring agents still may send anonymized telemetry to our ops team, but we can reduce that for EU-only plans. We'll share the inventory and flag which subprocessors will touch EU-pinned data.
[06:50] Tom: Do you use any troubleshooting tools that spin up ephemeral workers in US zones?
[06:58] Samir: For hosted, our fallback sometimes routes to nearest healthy zone in a cross-region failover. For strict EU-only SLAs we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can eliminate cross-region failover.

[07:30] Rachel: Can you walk through the flow for a single inference request for EU pinned tenant — from request ingress to logging and storage?
[07:40] Lina: Sure: 1) Ingress at EU endpoint (e.g., eu.redwood.ai) 2) Routing layer maps to EU-only inference fleet 3) KV cache (if used) is provisioned in EU cluster 4) Tokens and ephemeral caches live in memory on EU GPUs; we do not persist KV to US. 5) Output may be logged to customer-configured object storage within EU buckets; audit logs are stored in EU log storage for pinned tenants.
[08:20] Rachel: And what about third-party content moderation or safety services you call — e.g., if you use an external moderation model, does that spin data out of region?
[08:35] Samir: We try to use in-region moderation chains. If a specific moderating subprocess is outside EU, we can either disable that chain for your tenant or run the moderation on our in-region model variants.

[09:00] Priya: Regarding SCCs and transfer mechanisms — do you accept SCCs on the DPA or do you require additional safeguards? Our legal prefers SCCs plus technical controls.
[09:12] Ava: We support SCCs and have model clauses in our DPA. For extra safeguards, we layer contractual SCCs with technical controls like region pinning, encryption-at-rest with customer keys, and strict subprocessor rules. We'll have legal align on specific clause language.

[09:40] Tom: How do you prove where data was processed? We need evidence for auditors that student PII never left EU.
[09:50] Lina: We can provide an access log export with region tags and compute node IDs, plus attestation letters for the pinned tenant config. For Dedicated/Private we can provide SANDBOX audit logs that your team can scrape directly.
[10:10] Rachel: Those logs — are they signed or tamper-evident? We want immutable auditability.
[10:18] Samir: We support write-once storage with object-level immutability in EU buckets and we store cryptographic hashes of logs in a separate control plane ledger. For the strongest guarantee, Private deployment gives you full possession of logs.

[11:00] Priya: A tricky ask from procurement: they want a clause that prevents Redwood from engaging any subprocessor in a country outside the EEA for the EU-pinned workload without prior written consent. Is that contractually feasible?
[11:16] Ava: We can add that as a restriction in the DPA for EU-pinned scopes. We'll need to confirm operationally which subprocessors we'd need to exclude; some global observability vendors only have US regions. For those we can swap to EU-only partners at additional cost.

[11:40] Tom: On backups, do you do cross-region replication by default? Sounds like you can disable that for EU-pinned projects?
[11:48] Lina: Correct. Default for hosted is cross-region replication for resilience, but we can set a tenant to single-region replication with snapshots restricted to EU. That does increase recovery RTO risk. We can also do daily encrypted snapshots retained in EU.

[12:20] Rachel: What about metadata that might leak location tags — e.g., model run timings or region IDs. We need all PII-free in control plane.
[12:35] Samir: We can scrub or tokenized identifiers in the control plane. For telemetry we can send aggregated metrics only.

[13:00] Priya: Let's talk KMS details again. If we provide our own keys in an EU KMS, does Redwood ever get plaintext?
[13:10] Lina: No. With customer-managed keys (CMK) Redwood never receives plaintext. We wrap objects client-side or in the data plane with envelope encryption using your keys. Decryption happens only within the EU data plane and only when the HSM returns a decryption token.
[13:30] Tom: How are temporary worker nodes authorized to use the key? Is it via a short-lived role?
[13:36] Samir: Yes, we provision short-lived credentials and RBACed service identities. Key usage requires signed requests and token validation via our KMS proxy, again restricted to EU endpoints for pinned projects.

[14:10] Rachel: For the escrow scenario, would Redwood ever be able to decrypt outside a court order? I.e., under what conditions would Redwood access keys?
[14:22] Ava: Any Redwood access to escrowed keys would be governed by the escrow agreement and require dual sign-off, legal process, and audit trail. We can include conditions such as "customer bankruptcy" or "court order" and require customer consent for maintenance operations. We'll capture this in the KMS addendum.

[15:00] Priya: We need an SLA clause that if Redwood's EU region is unavailable, failovers must respect geo-fencing and can only failover to another EU region.
[15:10] Samir: For hosted, cross-region failover can sometimes cross into US for resilience; we can restrict failover to EU-only regions under a geo-fencing policy. That is a configuration for enterprise tenants and will be part of the tenant routing policy.

[16:00] Tom: What about logging retention limits per GDPR? We need automatic deletion after X months for PII logs.
[16:10] Lina: We support configurable retention policies per log type and can enforce deletion workflows. We'll provide a sample retention policy in the next steps.

[17:00] Rachel: A few practical things: 1) Please provide the up-to-date subprocessor inventory and flag any non-EU subprocessors 2) Provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate if available 3) Provide sample DPA language for SCCs and KMS addendum 4) Provide a sample tenant config for EU-only pinning and backup settings
[17:25] Ava: Absolutely. We'll push those docs after the call.

[18:00] Priya: One more legal nuance — do you offer a data processing location warranty? We want the DPA to include that data will be processed only in EU for the pinned scope, except for explicit maintenance windows.
[18:13] Ava: We can add that warranty with defined exceptions and notice periods for maintenance. For hosted we add exception language for emergency failover; for Dedicated/Private exceptions will be narrower.

[19:00] Samir: Quick tech deep dive: our runtime's KV cache is in-memory by default and not persisted. But we do persist model cache shards to object storage for warm startup. For EU pinning we ensure shard storage is in EU buckets.
[19:30] Tom: What about third-party model providers, like if you surface an open model that requires fetching weights — are model artifacts pulled from public repos?
[19:40] Lina: Model artifacts in our catalog are mirrored in-region for pinned tenants. We control the model artifact mirrors and can host them in EU registries for your tenant to avoid outbound fetches.

[20:10] Rachel: Are there any monitoring agents that phone home to Redwood US endpoints?
[20:18] Samir: We have optional monitoring telemetry that by default goes to our central ops. For EU-only we can configure telemetry to stay in-region and provide you a direct read-only view.

[21:00] Priya: Auditors may ask for evidence of physical location of hardware — can Redwood provide supplier attestations for the data centers?
[21:10] Ava: For cloud providers we provide provider region attestations (e.g., AWS eu-west-1). For Dedicated on-prem variants we can provide host-level attestations and supplier SOC reports where available.

[22:00] Tom: For SaaS connectors, e.g., if we use Redwood to index our LMS content, where does the connector run?
[22:10] Lina: Connectors can run in your VPC or via a secure connector that we host. For EU-only use, we recommend running connectors in your VPC so data never leaves your network unless you permit it.

[23:00] Rachel: On retention deletion proof, can you provide deletion receipts?
[23:08] Samir: We can emit signed deletion events and put them in an audit bucket. That can be part of the retention policy setup in the tenant config.

[24:00] Priya: Quick question from contract team — is Redwood willing to accept liability carveouts if a subprocessor breaches?
[24:10] Ava: We'll discuss indemnity language. We typically require flow-down obligations to subprocessors and will take liability for Redwood's negligence. Exact wording is negotiable.

[25:00] Tom: A specific scenario: a student record processed for a year is accidentally exported in a debug payload to a US log by a Redwood internal tool. What's the incident flow?
[25:15] Samir: Incident flow: detection alert -> containment -> preserve artifacts -> notify customer per SLA (we have an incident response playbook) -> forensic review. For EU-pinned we escalate to a special comms channel and legal team. We'll provide the playbook extract.

[26:00] Rachel: On encryption-at-rest, is everything AES-256?
[26:05] Lina: Yes AES-256 (or equivalent) for disk encryption and envelope encryption for objects. TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit.

[27:00] Priya: Are you doing any pseudonymization support? Could Redwood run a tokenization layer?
[27:10] Samir: We have integrations that can tokenize PII pre-ingest. For strict use-cases customers run tokenization client-side and send tokens to Redwood.

[28:00] Ava: Quick breakpoint — want to recap the contractual asks?
[28:05] Priya: Yes: updated subprocessor list, KMS addendum, SCC-enabled DPA, SOC2 + ISO artifacts, tenant config for EU-only with sample infra-as-code.
[28:18] Ava: Got it. We'll follow up.

[29:00] [Rapid-fire technical Q&A — transcription may lose words, some names slightly off]
[29:10] Tom: Are snapshots encrypted with separate keys?
[29:14] Samir: Yes, snapshot keys can be different from data keys; both manageable via KMS.
[29:30] Rachel: What about logging of admin console actions?
[29:35] Lina: Admin console actions are logged with user, timestamp, IP and action; we provide exportable audit logs.

[31:00] Priya: Can you restrict Redwood engineer access to EU-only tenant data? We want role separation and a strict allowlist.
[31:10] Ava: Yes, we have role-based access controls and we can apply least-privileged engineer roles. For high-sensitivity tenants we add jump-hosts and require escalation approvals.

[33:00] Tom: Any compliance-based skews we should know (e.g., data residency vs processing — some EU regs treat processing location differently)?
[33:10] Samir: We recommend treating the processing location as where compute occurs; we'll document compute node locality and the associated logs for auditors.

[35:00] Rachel: On SCCs, will Redwood accept our proposed amendments around subprocessors?
[35:08] Priya: (interjecting) We'll mark them up and share.
[35:15] Ava: Happy to review redlines.

[36:00] Samir: There was a question earlier about emergency access — we can implement a sealed escrow with dual-key release and a time-limited access window.
[36:15] Rachel: Would that be automated or manual? We prefer manual with explicit customer approval where possible.
[36:22] Lina: It can be constrained to manual release with legal sign-off.

[38:00] Tom: On observability stacks, can you swap to EU-only providers?
[38:08] Samir: Yes, we can use EU-only logging and tracing partners, but there may be a delta in retention or features. We'll provide options.

[40:00] Priya: Are you able to sign Data Processing Agreements that commit to region pinning as a contractual obligation?
[40:10] Ava: Yes — we'll include region pinning in the DPA scope and enumerated exceptions.

[42:00] Rachel: What evidence will you provide to auditors?
[42:08] Lina: We'll provide tenant config export, log export (with signed hashes), infrastructure region attestations, DPA with SCCs, and SOC 2 reports.

[44:00] Tom: Are there any limitations to model types for EU pinning — e.g., some quantized variants require specific CPU/GPU that only exist in US regions?
[44:15] Samir: Good callout. Some very specialized hardware (certain inference accelerators) may be region-limited. We'll produce a compatibility matrix for model families vs region availability.

[46:00] Priya: Let's talk timeline — procurement wants this in place before Oct 31. Is that possible for a pilot?
[46:10] Ava: For pilot (EU pinning + CMK) we can spin an enterprise pilot in 2-4 weeks, depending on legal turnaround for DPA and KMS addendum. Dedicated/Private will take longer (4-8 weeks).

[48:00] Rachel: Cost delta — what should we expect for EU-only constraints?
[48:08] Samir: Expect a modest premium for EU-only partners, and for Dedicated/Private the reserved capacity pricing applies. We'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.

[50:00] Priya: A few nitty bits — can you provide cipher suites, key rotation policy, and proof-of-rotation logs?
[50:10] Lina: Yes, we rotate keys per agreed schedule (customer-managed rotation optionally), and can provide rotation audit artifacts.

[52:00] Tom: Any blockers on your side to meet our requirements (SCCs, escrow, EU pinning)?
[52:10] Ava: No blockers — mostly tradeoffs and potential cost changes for non-standard subprocessors or escrow arrangements.

[54:00] Rachel: Great. Let's confirm next steps and owners.
[54:10] Ava: I'll send the SOC/ISO artifacts and the subprocessor list. Samir will send the tenant config and a pilot runbook. Lina will send the KMS addendum draft. Priya will send DPA redlines.
[54:30] Priya: We'll review and aim to sign pilot DPA by Oct 15.
[54:40] Tom: We'll also spin up a small engineering task to validate the tenant config.

[55:00] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[55:10] Rachel: Thanks, bye.
[55:12] All: Bye.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated subprocessor inventory and flag non-EU subprocessors
Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate
Redwood SE to provide tenant config JSON and infra-as-code snippet for EU-only pinning
Redwood legal to draft KMS addendum and sample DPA with SCCs
Customer to send DPA redlines and confirm pilot start date (aiming for Oct 15)
